rationale: A generic render-backend change. Skia surfaces are created under an explicit text raster policy (legacy by default, chromium = contrast 0 and gamma 1 for surfaces holding antialiased text), threaded through the frame, offscreen, scene and retained-layer targets and the capture paths; legacy equals a props-less surface, so no existing pixels change. Pulp continues to own these targets under the 2026-10-04 design-import refactor inheritance decision; Vellum inherits the change when the targets adopt the Vellum package. No design-import, Chromium, rendering or packaging authority moves.
tests: ctest --test-dir build -R 'a GPU surface carries its text raster policy into retained layers'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'a chromium surface changes how text rasterizes'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'an auto span on a chromium surface stays within the ink band'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'legacy surface props are the props a surface gets without any'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'text raster policy turns chromium when any text node is antialiased'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'text raster tuples are the measured contrast and gamma'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'text through a retained layer matches direct paint under each policy'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'the persistent scene target carries the surface'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'the widget gallery renders unchanged under the default policy'
